title: Tenant migration: retry attenuator + telemetry sanitizer to stop cascading 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During an enterprise tenant migration last week we observed correlated 5xx waves and long tail timeouts from the Hosted API across several regions. Symptoms included sustained connection pool exhaustion on front-door proxies, repeated in-flight retries observed as near-duplicate requests in traces, and KV cache churn on runtime nodes leading to serialization errors and 502s.

Impact:
- High customer-visible errors for a single migrating tenant (high SLA risk).
- Secondary impact on co-located tenants due to shared proxy resource exhaustion.

Hypothesis / Root causes: 
1) Migration traffic produced bursty replays from the client side (reconnects + automatic SDK retries) that lacked a tenant-scoped dedup/attenuation window. Many requests included identical request metadata (session IDs stripped by a proxy) so idempotency tokens collided or were lost.
2) Request metadata sanitization at the edge removed a tenant-scoped header we recently relied on to route repeat attempts to a local priority queue, so retries were treated as fresh requests and dispatched widely.
3) KV cache eviction thrashing occurred because the migration produced long sequences with large prefix histories; eviction led to repeated cold-start penalties and some deserialization races in the runtime, producing transient 5xxs.

Proposed mitigations (short term hotfixs):
- Deploy a retry-attenuator middleware at the edge proxy that implements a tenant-scoped sliding window (default 1s) to coalesce duplicate requests (configurable per-tenant).
- Reintroduce and normalize the tenant-routing header before any proto/proxy sanitization steps; add a defensive assertion that the header survives the sanitization pipeline.
- Add a telemetry sanitizer on traces to correlate near-duplicate requests using a computed fingerprint (method+path+body-hash+tenant) and surface the fingerprint in dashboards.
- Emergency runtime backoff: when KV eviction rate > 5% and tenant error rate spikes, route subsequent requests for that tenant to a low-memory, non-cached slowpath (small-model fallback) to avoid thrashing and restore service.

Longer-term actions:
- Upstream SDK guidance for migration flows: add jittered exponential backoff and a migration-mode toggle to prevent aggressive retries.
- Per-tenant admission control with burst credits and automatic cool-down windows.
- Runtime: add safer deserialization path for partially-evicted KV snapshots and stronger invariants on sequence metadata.
- Provide a runbook and a dashboard tile for migration events (tenant heatmap, KV eviction, fingerprint collision rate).

Acceptance criteria / Definition of done:
- Retry-attenuator middleware deployed to canary (us-east-1) and validated under synthetic migration traffic.
- Tenant-routing header assert + sanitizer in edge proxies → zero header loss across sanitization tests.
- Fingerprint-based telemetry shows a 90% reduction in replays surfaceable as duplicate-fingerprint counts within 1 hour for the canary tenant.
- Documentation and short SDK snippet published to Confluence and linked in customer escalation comms.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge hotfix PR and deploy middleware to canary subset (10% of front-door nodes) with the canary tenant bound.
2) Run 30m synthetic migration replay test (bench harness: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/runner/tenant-migrate-sim).
3) If canary metrics good (error rate drops by >=70% and KV eviction rate stabilizes), ramp to 50% then 100% over 3 hours.
4) Post-rollout: leave fingerprint telemetry enabled at full retention for 72 hours, then reduce to normal retention.

Notes on compatibility:
- Middleware is safe with Dedicated and Private when used in fronted Hosted proxies; for Dedicated we gate the feature behind "tenant_migration_mode" so customers can opt into the attenuator. Private deployments get a toggle and a short install script.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after oncall bridge. Initial triage indicates client-side replay combined with header sanitization. Assigned to Miguel for hotfix coordination.

2026-03-11 - Miguel Soto: Reproduced locally with migration simulator. Confirmed that edge sanitizer is dropping X-Redwood-Tenant-Routing under certain multipart uploads. Created runtime patch branch and started middleware prototype.

2026-03-12 - Olivia Chen (SRE review): Observed proxy connection pool exhaustion windows in us-east-1 between 03:12-03:40 UTC corresponding to the tenant burst. Recommend canary deploy to 2 nodes for further validation before wider rollout.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Soto: Hotfix PRs opened: infra#12345 and runtime#9876. Added unit tests for header preservation and fingerprint generation. Benchmark: attenuator adds ~0.4ms p50 to edge latency under baseline load.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Canary deployed to us-east-1. Ran synthetic migration with 5k concurrent simulated sessions. Duplicate-fingerprint rate fell 82% and 5xx volume for the migrating tenant dropped 78% during the window. KV eviction rate reduced from 9% -> 3.5%.

2026-03-15 - Product (K. Müller): Provided customer-facing summary and mitigation timeline to the account team. Drafted SDK guidance doc to discourage tight retry loops during migrations. Preparing postmortem draft.
